item.title: myAiVideos: An open-source pipeline for automated Chinese short-video production
item.description:
myAiVideos: An open-source pipeline for automated Chinese short-video production

myAiVideos is a new open-source engineering project designed for the automated production of Chinese-language short videos. It covers the full pipeline from topic discovery through creative generation, visuals, audio, and post-production, all the way to distribution.

🔍 Overview

The system is built as a modular platform that coordinates multiple AI models to handle generation and quality gating. Its architecture is designed to be decoupled, allowing individual layers of the pipeline to be independently replaced.

🧩 How it works

The project utilizes a seven-layer pipeline architecture:

  • L1: Topic
  • L2: Creative
  • L3: Visual
  • L4: Audio
  • L5: Post-production
  • L6: Distribution
  • L7: Optimization

Orchestration is managed by a FastAPI core, while a Java gateway acts as the platform governance layer. The gateway handles authentication, routing, circuit breaking, metering, and observability. Key technical mechanisms include:

  • Multi-model failover: The Java gateway aggregates DeepSeek, Qwen, and GLM using Resilience4j protection to automatically rotate failed providers.
  • Prompt anchoring: Maintains the visual identity of subjects across video segments.
  • CLIP gating: Rejects off-prompt keyframes early using text-image consistency checks.
  • Audio-video sync rescue: Employs a four-tier strategy involving audio tempo adjustments, video padding, and narration rewrites.

⚙️ Key details

The system provides full-stack observability by propagating trace_id across Java and Python environments and offering Langfuse call-tree visibility. Metering and rate limiting are handled via an AOP aspect that captures token and cost data without requiring code changes, aggregated by tenant. The production-ready setup includes SSE progress streaming, single-segment regeneration, and rolling log archives.

Component Technology / Model
Gateway Spring Boot 3.5, WebClient, Resilience4j, Caffeine, Prometheus
Text LLM DeepSeek
Multimodal Moderation Zhipu GLM-4V
Visuals Kling v2.5
Speech Synthesis Volcengine / MiniMax TTS
Transcription faster-whisper

🚀 Availability

myAiVideos is available as an open-source engineering project. It supports local execution using Docker Desktop version 24 or higher. Node.js 20 or higher is required for frontend development, while Python 3.11 or higher is needed for local execution without Docker or for running host tests. Health endpoints are available for the Python API, Java Gateway, and Frontend.

#OpenSource #VideoGeneration #FastAPI #Java #AIModels

Source: myccarl/ai-shortVideo-pipeline

item.title: Java 17 Spring Boot project implements RAG agent with hybrid search and observability
item.description:
Java 17 Spring Boot project implements RAG agent with hybrid search and observability

This update describes a Java 17 AI agent service built on Spring Boot 3.5 and LangChain4j 0.34. Designed for enterprise knowledge Q&A and intelligent customer service, the project implements a complete engineering pipeline that covers document ingestion, hybrid retrieval, and offline evaluation.

🔍 Overview

The system focuses on production-grade reliability, addressing common challenges like imprecise recall, uncontrolled costs, and lack of observability. It is not just a prompt demo; it features a full stack including semantic caching, multi-model routing, and end-to-end monitoring.

🧩 How it works

The request flow handles multiple scenarios to balance accuracy and cost:

  • Caching: A request first checks the semantic cache; if a match is found, it returns immediately to reduce API costs.
  • Processing: Unmatched queries trigger a ReAct loop or Adaptive RAG (query routing, rewriting, multi-turn retrieval) combined with tool calling.
  • Long Context: A LongContextManager handles extended sessions via sliding windows and summary compression.
  • Delivery: Results are written back to the cache and delivered using Server-Sent Events (SSE).

⚙️ Key details

  • Hybrid Search: Combines Milvus vector search and BM25 keyword search, fused using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) with a k=60 constant.
  • Semantic Cache: Uses embedding cosine similarity with a 0.92 threshold and a 24-hour time-to-live (TTL).
  • Evidence Gating: Validates evidence levels before answering; if evidence is insufficient, the system routes the query to a human operator.
  • Multi-model Routing: Routes requests across various providers including DeepSeek, Qwen, Doubao, Qwen3-Flash, and local Ollama instances.
  • Safety Measures: The ReAct loop includes safeguards against infinite loops, timeouts, and step count limits.
  • Observability: Integrates Micrometer, Prometheus, and Grafana to track latency across chat, retrieval, and ingestion stages.

Performance and Testing

Metric Value Context
FAQ Retrieval (R@1) 98.3% Multi-gold evaluation across 120 cases and 6 categories
Single Gold Baseline R@1 47.5% / R@5 62.5% Used for regression comparison between versions
FAQ Latency (P95) 181ms Multi-gold evaluation
Code Coverage 64% JaCoCo line coverage (exceeds the 45% gate)
Test Suite 372 Unit and integration tests

#Java #SpringBoot #RAG #AIAgents #LangChain4j

Source: 888newstep/ai-agent-platform

item.title: New Java Library for Qdrant Vector Search Engine Released
item.description:
New Java Library for Qdrant Vector Search Engine Released

A new Java library for the Qdrant vector search engine has been released, providing a high-level client with utility methods for interfacing with Qdrant. The library requires Java 8 or above and uses a low-level gRPC client internally to interact with Qdrant.

📦 Installation

To install the library, add the following lines to your build config file. Please ensure all necessary dependencies listed in the documentation are included in your project.

🛠️ How It Works

The client provides convenient methods and overloads for common operations, including:

  • Creating a new collection
  • Inserting vectors into a collection
  • Searching for similar vectors
  • Searching for similar vectors with filtering conditions

🔐 Configuration

Additional constructor overloads allow fine-grained control over the gRPC client configuration. For example, the following demonstrates how to configure a client to use TLS with certificate validation via the root CA and API key authentication.

🔄 Lifecycle Management

The client implements AutoCloseable, though it is typically created once and used for the application’s lifetime. When constructed by passing a ManagedChannel, the client does not shut down the channel on close by default. It can be configured to shut down the channel upon closing instead.

⏱️ Asynchronous Operations

All client methods return ListenableFuture<T>, enabling asynchronous workflows.

📚 Resources

Usage examples are available in the Qdrant documentation and API Reference.

#Java #Qdrant #VectorSearch #gRPC #ArtificialIntelligence

item.title: Reactor 3 Java Reactive Library Overview and Build Requirements
item.description:
Reactor 3 Java Reactive Library Overview and Build Requirements

Reactor 3 is a non-blocking Reactive Streams foundation for the JVM, implementing a Reactive Extensions-inspired API with efficient event streaming support.

⚙️ Key details

  • Reactor 3 requires Java 8 or higher to run.
  • Reactor 3 does not officially support nor target Android.
  • However, it should work fine with Android SDK 21 (Android 5.0) and above.
  • Since 3.3.x, the repository also contains reactor-tools, a Java agent aimed at helping with debugging of Reactor code.

🧩 How it works

Reactor functions as a Reactive Streams Publisher with basic flow operators. Its architecture includes:

  • Static factories on Flux: Allow for source generation from arbitrary callback types.
  • Instance methods: Allow for operational building, materialized on each subscription (such as Flux#subscribe()), or multicasting operations (such as Flux#publish and Flux#publishNext).

🚀 Availability and Build

The build process involves specific Java Development Kit (JDK) requirements due to support for Java Multi-Release JAR Files.

Requirement Detail
Classpath JDKs JDK 8, 9, and 21 must be available.
Toolchain Management Gradle Toolchains should automatically detect or provision the required JDKs.
Active Shell JDK Must be compatible with JDK 17 or higher for Antora to build successfully.
Missing JDK Errors Errors like No matching toolchains found for requested specification indicate a missing JDK that needs to be installed.

Documentation is generated in docs/build/site/index.html and in docs/build/distributions/reactor-core-<version>-docs.zip. If a PDF file is included in the generated docs zip, the -PforcePdf option must be specified, which requires the asciidoctor-pdf command to be available in the PATH.

#ReactiveProgramming #Java #JVM #Reactor #ReactiveStreams

Source: reactor/reactor-core

item.title: A2A Java SDK releases client and server support for agent communication
item.description:
A2A Java SDK releases client and server support for agent communication

A new Java library has been released to support the execution of agentic applications as Agent2Agent (A2A) servers. This multi-module Maven library provides both client and server capabilities, enabling A2A agent communication across JSON-RPC, gRPC, and REST transports.

🧩 How it works

The library facilitates agent-to-agent interaction by implementing the A2A Protocol. For gRPC support, the project copies the a2a.proto file from the A2A specification repository into the spec-grpc/ project. The java_package option is adjusted to target the org.a2aproject.sdk.grpc package. Developers can regenerate the gRPC classes by building the module with the command mvn clean install -Dskip.protobuf.generate=false.

⚙️ Key details

  • Language Requirement: Java 17 or later is required.
  • Transport Protocols: Supports JSON-RPC, gRPC, and REST.
  • Licensing: The project is licensed under the Apache 2.0 License.
  • Documentation: Full documentation is available at a2aproject.github.io/a2a-java.

🚀 Availability and Integrations

Developers can add the A2A Java SDK reference server for JSON-RPC to their Maven projects. The SDK includes examples for cross-language integration, such as a Java A2A server communicating with a Python client, and a Java A2A client communicating with a Python server.

Feature Details
OpenTelemetry Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
JPA-backed task store Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
Kafka-based replicated queue manager Available as an optional add-on in the extras folder
Vert.x and Android HTTP clients Available as optional add-ons in the extras folder

Integrations with Java runtimes are documented in the Server Integrations section of the reference materials.

#Java #AIagents #A2A #Maven #gRPC

item.title: New Structural-Validation Evaluation Harness for Java LLM Codegen Service
item.description:
New Structural-Validation Evaluation Harness for Java LLM Codegen Service

📚 Introduction

A new structural-validation evaluation harness has been introduced for a Java LLM codegen service, designed to make A/B changes measurable and provide deterministic metrics instead of relying on demo screenshots or subjective assessments.

🔍 Overview

The harness implements a two-tier evaluation approach:

  • Runs benchmark prompts against a local Java service
  • Captures generated code through SSE
  • Evaluates outputs with deterministic structural checks
  • Optional browser execution smoke checks
  • Records raw JSON plus Markdown reports
  • Attributes tokens with per-run Prometheus counter windows

The most important finding was not a token percentage but a discovered issue: an earlier token result was polluted by Redis MessageWindowChatMemory carryover on a shared appId.

🧩 How it Works

The evaluation system operates through several components:

  • Kubernetes manifests serve Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B through vLLM
  • Infrastructure spans infra/azure (AKS/ACR/node pools) and infra/workloads (Terraform-managed inference/evaluation workloads)
  • A read-only authenticated GraphQL API queries both legacy Java reports and new serving runs
  • A bounded-concurrency benchmark records TTFT, p50/p95 latency, request/token throughput and structural quality

⚙️ Key Details

The structural pass@k evaluation found:

Metric Result
Structural pass@3 90.0% -> 90.0%
Total tokens 323,192 -> 317,785 (-1.7%)
CodeGen-stage input reduction ~18%

The harness identified a Java product bug: loadChatHistoryToMemory(...) returned before chatMemory.clear() when MySQL history was empty, causing prompt-composition diagnostics to reveal most of the CodeGen prompt was carried-over history.

Additional capabilities include:

  • Optional direct OpenAI-compatible inference reusing HTML evaluators and raw result format
  • Execution smoke checker validates known browser fixtures
  • One-shot repair path validates on a deterministic fixture
  • Replay / fixture mode validates offline report and evaluator paths
  • Failure taxonomy classifies report failures by layer

🚀 Availability

Documentation is available in three parts:

  • Part 1 deployment and recording guide
  • Part 2 Azure guide
  • Part 3 query and recording guide

Additional references:

  • RESULTS.md for full claim audit
  • Redis chat-memory carryover postmortem for incident write-up
  • LoRA/QLoRA SFT and held-out evaluation for deterministic data preparation and training provenance

💡 Why It Matters

The structural-validation pass@k differs from HumanEval-style evaluation:

  • It measures deterministic structural correctness, not functional correctness
  • Execution smoke validation serves as a thin second layer for narrow browser/build sanity, not full functional testing
  • The two layers are reported separately to avoid collapsing into one ambiguous pass number

Implementation tests are offline, and actual GPU deployment and performance measurements are pending. The sample data serves as a pipeline smoke fixture, with GPU training and quality gains remaining unverified.

#LLM #Evaluation #CodeGeneration #Java #DevOps #Kubernetes

Source: LING-6150/llm-codegen-eval

item.title: Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2
item.description:
Milvus Java SDK Splits Into Two Packages From v2.5.2

The Milvus Java SDK has been restructured starting with version 2.5.2. The SDK is now split into two separate packages: milvus-sdk-java and milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter. This change was made because BulkWriter requires a significant number of dependencies.

🧩 Available Packages

  • milvus-sdk-java: The core Milvus Java SDK package
  • milvus-sdk-java-bulkwriter: A separate package for BulkWriter functionality

⚙️ Key Details

The Milvus Java SDK has the following requirements:

  • Java 8 or higher
  • Build tools: Apache Maven or Gradle
  • SLF4J is required for logging purposes and must be added to the classpath

Developers can add the Milvus SDK to their projects using either:

  • Apache Maven
  • Gradle

🚀 Availability

For Spring Boot applications (Java 17+), the milvus-sdk-java-spring-boot-starter package automatically configures a MilvusClientV2 from milvus.* properties.

Examples for the Java SDK are available in the examples folder.

💡 Contributing

Contributors should:

  • Read the contribution guidelines first
  • Refer to the DEVELOPMENT.md file for development information

item.title: Kiro AI IDE and AWS Transform Enable Repeatable PHP‑to‑Java Migration
item.description:
Kiro AI IDE and AWS Transform Enable Repeatable PHP‑to‑Java Migration

A new AI‑enabled workflow lets teams move mature PHP applications to Java with a measurable, repeatable process.

🔍 Overview

  • “When your team moves a mature PHP application to Java, you gain stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling.”
  • “Kiro is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) that pairs an AI agent with your codebase to run multi‑step engineering tasks with you in the loop.”
  • “AWS Transform is the AWS agentic AI service for large‑scale migration and modernization, and it now integrates natively with Kiro.”

🧩 How it works

  • “The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight‑phase workflow.”
  • “This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it.”
  • “Everything here is packaged as skill files: versioned Markdown capability packages that encode the migration methodology (php-to-java-migration) and the discovery scanner workflow (php-model-discovery).”
  • “The engine is organized around a single principle: one shared brain, many projects.”
  • “At the top is a global .kiro/ layer that every project draws on.”
  • “A shared, global layer under .kiro/ holds two Skills, php-model-discovery (the scanner) and php-to-java-migration (the eight‑phase playbook), plus the core‑workflow.md Steering file.”

⚙️ Key details

  • “Kiro brings an AI agent into your editor to drive a migration step by step.”
  • “Open the repository root as a Kiro workspace and the skills activate automatically when you ask Kiro to migrate a PHP application.”
  • “Kiro then walks the eight‑phase workflow with explicit approval gates, so you review the discovery manifest, approve the rulebook, and sign off on each phase before the next begins.”
  • “Use Kiro to work through the code first: run the skill on one application, read the generated Java, and run the tests.”
  • “When you want to migrate more, AWS Transform runs the same methodology agentically with review at the checkpoints the skill defines.”
  • “Kiro handles one application at a time and suits first‑of‑a‑kind frameworks.”
  • “AWS Transform runs many applications as parallel jobs.”
  • “Both paths read the same skill files, so every rulebook fix made in Kiro improves the next AWS Transform run, and vice versa.”
  • “The scanner is discover‑models.php, a single‑file, dependency‑free PHP command‑line tool that doesn’t execute the target code.”
  • “It only reads source text as tokens, so it runs against apps of your choice whether its dependencies are installed.”
  • “Each per‑project folder holds its own PHP source, Java output, and spec sub‑folder under .kiro/specs/, so improving the methodology once lets every project inherit the gain.”

🚀 Availability

  • “You start with an open repository, so you can run the engine yourself rather than read about it.”
  • “Open the repository root as a Kiro workspace and the skills activate automatically when you ask Kiro to migrate a PHP application.”
  • “Through that integration, you can hand AWS Transform the same skill files that govern an interactive Kiro session, so discovery before translation, the parity harness as referee, and ‘fix the loop, not the code’ apply to an autonomous run.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling are achieved by moving to Java.
  • An eight‑phase, parity‑first pipeline guarantees that the Java port matches the original PHP specification before it is accepted.
  • The same skill files power both an interactive, single‑application workflow (Kiro) and a large‑scale, parallel workflow (AWS Transform), ensuring consistency across projects.

#PHP #Java #AI #Migration #AWS

Source: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro | Amazon Web Services
